title: August and the Current
premise: Petra Voss, a salvage diver who has spent a decade erasing himself from every record that matters, is hired to strip a sunken barge in the Verren River—a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to touch. Among the silt he finds a sealed chest bearing the crest of Kaldavia, a nation erased from maps twenty years ago, and inside it documents proving the purge that destroyed Kaldavia was orchestrated by men who now run the republic. Hunted by the navy's fixer, Captain Ilse Marrow, Petra flees east with a disgraced archivist named Sela and the chest itself, racing to cross the Ashen Range before snowfall seals the passes for winter. At the border monastery of Saint Ovelun, Petra must choose between burning the evidence to save his own skin and delivering it to the last free press beyond the mountains—an act that will finally give him a name worth having. He delivers it, at the cost of nearly everything he carried, and for the first time stops moving.
about_author: Wren Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent six years mapping riverbeds along contested borders before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose survival depends on staying unreadable.

chapters.title: The Bottom of the Verren
chapters.summary: Petra dives the forbidden wreck alone at dawn, establishing his methodical, detached competence and his rule: take salvage, leave no trace of himself. He finds a chest too heavy to raise and marks it, telling no one. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Contract with No Signature
chapters.summary: In the port town of Halden's Reach, Petra negotiates payment through a broker who never gives names, and notices navy patrol boats sweeping the river with unusual instruments. His instinct says leave; his empty purse says dive again. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the tug-of-war between caution and need.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Petra raises the chest in a night dive, nearly drowning when a cable snags. Inside: ledgers, letters, and a seal of Kaldavia—the dead nation. He understands instantly why the navy wants the river silent. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Captain Marrow
chapters.summary: Ilse Marrow arrives in Halden's Reach asking quiet questions about divers. Petra watches her work from a tavern corner—patient, courteous, terrifying—and realizes she has his broker's ledger. He packs that night. POV: alternating Petra and Marrow. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes visible.

chapters.title: Sela of the Burned Archive
chapters.summary: Fleeing upriver, Petra is caught by Sela Iven, an exiled archivist who recognizes the Kaldavian seal and begs to come—she can read the ciphered pages. He refuses; she follows anyway. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: two people who trust no one recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Krast
chapters.summary: At a checkpoint bridge, Petra bribes his way across but sees Marrow's agents photographing travelers. Sela deciphers her first page: a list of Kaldavian officials and their fates, signed by a name still powerful today. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the past acquiring teeth.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Hiding in an abandoned smelter, Petra tells Sela about the brother he lost in the purges' aftermath and why he stopped using his real name. For the first time the chest feels personal rather than dangerous. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: grief surfacing after years underwater.

chapters.title: Marrow's Net
chapters.summary: Marrow closes the river towns, posting rewards and quietly executing a smuggler who saw too much. Her POV reveals she isn't loyal to the navy—she's protecting someone whose name is on the pages. POV: Marrow. Emotional beat: the antagonist given a human wound.

chapters.title: The Road Through Vetch
chapters.summary: Petra and Sela buy passage with a caravan of salt traders, blending in among strangers for the first time. A child asks Petra his name and he almost answers honestly. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed and flinched from.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: A caravan hand sells their location. Marrow's men raid the waystation at night; Petra and Sela escape into the hills with the chest but lose their money and their cover. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: paranoia reasserting itself over fragile trust.

chapters.title: The First Snowline
chapters.summary: High on the foothills, they see early snow on the Ashen Range—weeks ahead of schedule. A shepherd warns the northern pass will close within the month. The deadline becomes real. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: time turning into an adversary.

chapters.title: What the Pages Say
chapters.summary: By firelight, Sela finishes deciphering the core document: proof the republic's founding council sold Kaldavia's fleet to its enemies. One signer still holds office. Petra realizes the chest could topple a government—or get them both killed quietly. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: The Monastery of Saint Ovelun
chapters.summary: They shelter at a mountain monastery where monks once served Kaldavia's church. The abbot recognizes the seal and offers sanctuary—but also sends word down-mountain, and not only to God. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: refuge with a hidden price.

chapters.title: Marrow Ascending
chapters.summary: Marrow climbs into the range with a small team, abandoning official channels because her superiors want the matter buried, not solved. Her private motive sharpens: her father's signature is on the pages. POV: Marrow. Emotional beat: duty and blood pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Pass of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Petra and Sela attempt the high pass early to outrun both weather and Marrow. A storm catches them; they shelter in a cave where Petra admits he's been running since the purges—not hiding, punishing himself. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: confession in the white silence.

chapters.title: Caught Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Marrow intercepts them near the summit ridge. She takes the chest but hesitates to kill them—and Sela reads aloud the page naming Marrow's father, offering her the truth she's been chasing. POV: Marrow. Emotional beat: the hunter at her own crossroads.

chapters.title: The Fall
chapters.summary: A cornice collapses in the standoff. Marrow saves Sela from the drop, then vanishes downslope with the chest, leaving Petra broken-armed and furious. The storm seals the pass behind them all. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: despair at the summit of the world.

chapters.title: Descent Without a Map
chapters.summary: Petra and Sela descend the far side half-frozen, guided by the abbot's cryptic directions to the last free press beyond the border. Petra, unable to dive or fight, must rely entirely on Sela—inverting their roles. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: dependence as a kind of grace.

chapters.title: The Border of Paper
chapters.summary: At a remote customs hut, they forge transit papers using skills from Sela's archive years. Marrow appears—not to arrest them, but to return the chest: she has read it all and chooses truth over her family's name. POV: Marrow. Emotional beat: the antagonist's redemption, paid in exile.

chapters.title: Beyond the Range
chapters.summary: They cross into the free territories and reach the underground press in the town of Velin Ost, where printers weep over the Kaldavian pages. Officers of the old regime gather to verify the documents. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the weight lifting, terror replacing it.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Publishing means Petra's identity enters the record—he can never be invisible again, and reprisals will follow. He signs the testimony with his true name, the first time in ten years. Marrow stands witness. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally paid forward.

chapters.title: August and the Current
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the revelations shake the republic, and the navy's silence cracks open. Petra stays in Velin Ost, teaching divers to read wrecks honestly, the chest enshrined in a public archive. Stopping, he discovers, costs nothing at all. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: arrival—identity, belonging, rest.
